message: IAM Role gh-apply does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess policy attached.
status_detail: IAM Role gh-apply does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess policy attached.

analytic.name: IAM role does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess managed policy attached

finding_info.desc:
**IAM roles** (excluding service roles) are evaluated for attachment of the AWS-managed `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` policy.

This policy grants unrestricted access to all Amazon Bedrock actions and resources.
finding_info.title: IAM role does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess managed policy attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege**: replace `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` with a custom policy granting only the specific Bedrock actions required.

Use **permissions boundaries** and **SCPs** to limit the scope of Bedrock permissions. Regularly review access with **IAM Access Analyzer** to identify and remove unused privileges.

risk_details:
The `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` policy grants broad permissions across all Bedrock resources. If a role with this policy is compromised, an attacker could:
- Invoke any model to exfiltrate data or generate harmful content
- Modify guardrails, logging, and security configurations
- Incur significant costs through unrestricted model invocations

message: IAM Role gh-apply does not have BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess or AgentRegistryFullAccess policy attached.
status_detail: IAM Role gh-apply does not have BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess or AgentRegistryFullAccess policy attached.

analytic.name: IAM role does not have the AWS-managed Bedrock AgentCore full access policies attached

finding_info.desc:
**IAM roles** (excluding service roles) are evaluated for attachment of the AWS-managed `BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess` or `AgentRegistryFullAccess` policies.

These policies grant unrestricted access to the `bedrock-agentcore` and `agent-registry` actions respectively.
finding_info.title: IAM role does not have the AWS-managed Bedrock AgentCore full access policies attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc: Apply **least privilege**: replace `BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess` and `AgentRegistryFullAccess` with custom policies granting only the specific actions a workload calls, scoped to specific resource ARNs. Keep the control-plane actions that reconfigure gateways and policy engines separate from the invoke actions agents need at runtime.

risk_details:
**Full AgentCore access** is not only the ability to invoke agents. It includes `UpdateGateway`, `PutResourcePolicy` and the policy-engine calls.

So one compromised credential can disable a gateway authorizer, flip a policy engine to `LOG_ONLY`, or grant itself cross-account access, and then invoke the agent it just unguarded.

message: IAM Role gh-apply allows both bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentSession and bedrock-agentcore:ProcessPayment.
status_detail: IAM Role gh-apply allows both bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentSession and bedrock-agentcore:ProcessPayment.

unmapped.notes: Only an explicit `Deny` on `Resource: "*"` without `Condition` or `NotResource` cancels an `Allow`, so a role allowed each action on a different payment manager is still reported as FAIL. Roles allowing neither action are not reported.

analytic.name: IAM role does not both open and execute Bedrock AgentCore payments

finding_info.desc: **Bedrock AgentCore payments** split a transaction into `CreatePaymentSession`, which establishes the reviewable terms, and `ProcessPayment`, which executes it. This check verifies no IAM role (excluding service roles) is allowed both actions, evaluating its attached and inline policies together.
finding_info.title: IAM role does not both open and execute Bedrock AgentCore payments
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc: Split `CreatePaymentSession` and `ProcessPayment` across two IAM roles so the principal that proposes a transaction cannot execute it. Avoid `bedrock-agentcore:*` and prefix wildcards on payment roles, and add an explicit `Deny` on the action the role must never perform.

risk_details:
The agent that opens a **payment session** should not be the principal that executes the payment.

When one role holds both, a **prompt injection** or a stolen credential completes an unreviewed transaction end to end: it sets its own amount and payee, then charges it, with no second principal in the path to reject the terms. Money movement is not reversible by an IAM change afterward.

status_detail: No CloudTrail trails enabled with logging were found.

AWS-Account-Security-Onboarding: Enable as part of Organization trail

analytic.name: Region has at least one CloudTrail trail logging

finding_info.desc: **AWS CloudTrail** has at least one trail with `logging` enabled in every region. A **multi-region trail** or a regional trail counts for coverage in that region.
finding_info.title: Region has at least one CloudTrail trail logging
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Use a **multi-region CloudTrail trail** or per-region trails so `logging` is active in every region, including unused ones.

Centralize logs, enforce **least privilege** to log stores, and add **defense-in-depth** with encryption, integrity validation, and retention. Continuously monitor trail health to catch gaps.

risk_details:
Missing coverage in any region creates **visibility gaps**.

Attackers can use lesser-monitored regions to run API actions, hide **unauthorized changes**, and exfiltrate data without audit trails, weakening **detective controls**, hindering **forensics**, and delaying response (confidentiality and integrity).

message: Network ACL acl-0197d2ede7aac2ed8 has every port open to the Internet.
status_detail: Network ACL acl-0197d2ede7aac2ed8 has every port open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Network ACL does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to any port

finding_info.desc: **VPC network ACLs** with **inbound entries** that permit traffic from `0.0.0.0/0` to any port (any protocol) are identified at the subnet boundary.
finding_info.title: Network ACL does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to any port
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Adopt a **deny-by-default** NACL posture: block `0.0.0.0/0` and allow only required ports from trusted CIDRs. Apply **least privilege** using security groups for fine-grained access, with NACLs as coarse stateless filters. Review and prune rules regularly, and employ **defense in depth** with monitoring and alerting.

risk_details: Allowing Internet-wide ingress at the subnet layer enables broad port scanning and unsolicited connections. Attackers can probe and exploit exposed services, risking data disclosure and tampering (confidentiality, integrity) and causing outages via floods or brute-force (availability). Any security group lapse then lacks a compensating control.

message: EMR Account has Block Public Access enabled.
status_detail: EMR Account has Block Public Access enabled.

analytic.name: EMR account has Block Public Access enabled

finding_info.desc: Amazon EMR account-level **Block Public Access** configuration is assessed per Region. When `BlockPublicSecurityGroupRules` is enabled, clusters cannot use security groups that allow inbound public sources (`0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0`) except on permitted ports.
finding_info.title: EMR account has Block Public Access enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Keep EMR **Block Public Access** enabled and minimize exceptions; allow only required ports and restrict sources.

Apply **least privilege** on security groups, place clusters in private subnets, and use bastion hosts or Session Manager. Combine with **VPC** controls and monitoring for **defense in depth**.

risk_details:
Public EMR-facing rules enable Internet reachability to cluster nodes and UIs, inviting brute force and remote exploits.

Attackers can exfiltrate job data, alter processing, or pivot into the VPC, degrading **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability** through data theft, tampering, and service disruption.

message: EventBridge event bus default does not allow cross-account access.
status_detail: EventBridge event bus default does not allow cross-account access.

unmapped.notes: This check supports the `trusted_account_ids` configuration in config.yaml to allow specific cross-account access without triggering a finding.

analytic.name: AWS EventBridge event bus does not allow cross-account access

finding_info.desc:
**EventBridge event bus** has a **resource policy** that grants **cross-account event delivery** to principals outside the account, including broad or public access.

Focus is on buses whose policies permit external accounts to send events.
finding_info.title: AWS EventBridge event bus does not allow cross-account access
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** on the event bus resource policy: allow only specific account IDs or org scope (e.g., `aws:PrincipalOrgID`) and avoid wildcard `Principal` or `*`.

Constrain rules to trusted senders using the `account` field and vetted sources, and add monitoring/throttling for **defense in depth**.

risk_details: **Cross-account event injection** can erode **integrity** and **availability**. Spoofed events may trigger rules and invoke downstream targets, causing unintended actions, data exposure via targets, lateral movement through over-privileged roles, and cost or service disruption from event floods.

message: EventBridge event bus default is not exposed to everyone.
status_detail: EventBridge event bus default is not exposed to everyone.

analytic.name: AWS EventBridge event bus policy does not allow public access

finding_info.desc: EventBridge event bus resource policy is evaluated for **public access**, such as a `Principal: "*"` or overly broad conditions that allow any AWS account to publish events or manage rules on the bus.
finding_info.title: AWS EventBridge event bus policy does not allow public access
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** resource policies: limit principals to specific accounts or your organization, and constrain actions and event attributes (e.g., `source`, `detail-type`). Avoid `Principal: "*"`.

Use **defense in depth** with rule patterns that include the expected `account`. Monitor policy changes and bus activity.

risk_details: Publicly accessible event buses enable **event injection** and unauthorized rule changes, undermining **integrity** and enabling **lateral movement**. Attackers can trigger downstream targets, causing **data exposure**, service disruption, and unexpected **costs** through high-volume events.

status_detail: GuardDuty in region us-east-1 has issues: detector not enabled; the delegated administrator status could not be determined.

analytic.name: GuardDuty has delegated admin configured and is enabled in all regions with organization auto-enable

finding_info.desc: **Amazon GuardDuty** has a delegated administrator configured at the organization level, detectors are enabled in all opted-in regions, and organization auto-enable is active for new member accounts.
finding_info.title: GuardDuty has delegated admin configured and is enabled in all regions with organization auto-enable
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Configure a **delegated administrator** for GuardDuty via AWS Organizations. Enable GuardDuty detectors in **all opted-in regions** and configure **auto-enable** to automatically enroll new member accounts. This ensures consistent threat detection coverage across the entire organization.

risk_details: Without org-wide **Amazon GuardDuty** configuration, gaps can occur where detectors are enabled in some regions but not others, delegated admin is inconsistent, and new accounts are not auto-enrolled. This fragments **threat visibility**, delays **incident response**, and allows adversaries to exploit unmonitored regions or accounts for **lateral movement** and **data exfiltration**.

message: GuardDuty is not enabled.
status_detail: GuardDuty is not enabled.

AWS-Account-Security-Onboarding: Enable as part of central configuration for Organization
Confirm that events are present in SIEM
Apply suppression filters to disable useless findings
Include in process of incident response based on events

analytic.name: GuardDuty detector is enabled and not suspended

finding_info.desc: **Amazon GuardDuty** detector existence and health are evaluated per Region. It identifies where GuardDuty isn't enabled for the account, where a detector has no status, or where a detector is configured but `suspended`.
finding_info.title: GuardDuty detector is enabled and not suspended
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Runtime Behavior Analysis
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enable and keep **GuardDuty** active in all supported Regions and accounts under a delegated admin. Turn on relevant protection plans and auto-enroll new accounts. Avoid `suspended` detectors, enforce **least privilege** for admins, and integrate findings into response for **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Without active **GuardDuty**, threats in CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS, S3, EKS, EBS, and Lambda can go unnoticed. Attackers can exfiltrate data, move laterally, and mine crypto, degrading confidentiality, integrity, and availability-especially in unmonitored Regions.

message: Root user in the account wasn't accessed in the last 1 days.
status_detail: Root user in the account wasn't accessed in the last 1 days.

analytic.name: AWS account root user has not been used in the last day

finding_info.desc: **AWS IAM root user** activity is assessed by inspecting `last-used` timestamps for the root password and access keys. The finding indicates when the root identity has been used recently for console or programmatic access.
finding_info.title: AWS account root user has not been used in the last day
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Minimize `root` usage by applying **least privilege** with admin roles or federated SSO and temporary credentials.
- Enforce **MFA** on root
- Avoid or remove root access keys
- Require multi-person approval
- **Monitor and alert** on any root sign-in
- Use org guardrails for **defense in depth**

risk_details:
Recent **root usage** expands blast radius:
- Data exfiltration (**confidentiality**)
- Policy/key tampering (**integrity**)
- Resource deletion and billing changes (**availability**)
Routine use reduces anomaly visibility and eases **account takeover** impact.

message: AWS policy AWSTrustedAdvisorServiceRolePolicy is attached but does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges.
status_detail: AWS policy AWSTrustedAdvisorServiceRolePolicy is attached but does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges.

analytic.name: Attached AWS-managed IAM policy does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges

finding_info.desc: **IAM AWS-managed policies** attached to identities are inspected for statements that allow `Action:'*'` on `Resource:'*'`-i.e., full administrative `*:*` permissions
finding_info.title: Attached AWS-managed IAM policy does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege**: avoid attaching AWS-managed policies that grant `*:*`.
- Use **customer-managed, scoped policies** per role
- Enforce **separation of duties** and **permissions boundaries**
- Prefer **temporary, time-bound elevation** for emergencies with MFA
- Regularly review access and use conditions to constrain context

risk_details:
**Unrestricted `*:*` access** enables any action on any resource, risking:
- Data exfiltration (**confidentiality**)
- Unauthorized changes and policy tampering (**integrity**)
- Service deletion or shutdown (**availability**)
Attackers can disable logging, create backdoor principals, and expand lateral movement.
